page.overview:
Who is Abraxas?

When the Galactus of Earth-616 died, Abraxas emerged from Eternity's core. Abraxas soon began to cut a swath of terror throughout various alternate realities and murdered every alternate reality variant of Galactus he came across. Abraxas used the head of Galactus of Earth-1462 to target and home in on Earth-616's Earth; he also planted a mole in the form of a variant of the dead Herald Nova. On the Moon, Abraxas attacked Uatu the Watcher and stole half of his signature medallion.

Abraxas taunted the Fantastic Four with the inevitability of his arrival, enticing the team to search for the Ultimate Nullifier, the clues to the location of which were scattered among alternate realities. Ultimately, the Four found the Ultimate Nullifier when Abraxas suddenly appeared and stole it from them. Abraxas called forth an army of Novas to attack Earth and the Fantastic Four held no hope of defeating him. Instead, Franklin Richards, the son of the Four members Mister Fantastic and the Invisible Woman, combined his cosmic powers with those of his sister, Valeria, to reconstitute Galactus and thus restored balance to Eternity, at the cost of burning out his own powers. Galactus took the Ultimate Nullifier from Abraxas, giving it to Mister Fantastic who used the weapon, destroying himself and Abraxas. The result served to recreate a reality in which Abraxas never existed, and since all that was had ended, all that is was realigned, allowing Mister Fantastic to survive along with all those who died in Abraxas' reign of terror.

Restored in the Eighth Cosmos, Abraxas was used as a "bomb" entity by his father, Eternity. Abraxas was sent to destroy Oblivion but failed to finish him off. In retaliation, Oblivion unleashed Eternity's enemy, Hadad, who was trapped within Oblivion's realm, the storm god killed Oblivion. Using the mutant goddess Storm as a host, Eternity hid Abraxas in the Storm Sanctuary. In the battle against Hadad, Eternity summoned Abraxas and they combined their power with Storm to kill Hadad.
